Define the equivariant ring of differential operators to be the graded $k[\hbar]$ -algebra

(2.9)

$R_{eq}:=k[z^{\mu}]\otimes\mathrm{Sym}\ \mathcal{A}^{2}_{0},$

where $z^{\mu}$ are formal variables of degree $0$ indexed by $\mu\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\Sigma_{eq,+}$ , subject to the relation

(2.10)

$az^{\mu}=z^{\mu}(a+\hbar\langle\mu,\bar{a}\rangle),$

where $\bar{a}\in\mathfrak{t}$ denotes the image of $a\in\mathcal{A}_{0}^{2}$ under the projection map in the quantization exact sequence.

Here, the $k[\hbar]$ -module structure on $R_{eq}$ comes from the quantization exact sequence. Although $R_{eq}$ is not commutative, one can show that there exists a well-defined localization
$R_{eq,reg}:=R[(1-z^{\mu})^{-1}]$ obtained by inverting $(1-z^{\mu})$ for $\mu\in\Sigma_{eq,+}$ , see [KMP21, Lemma 3.4].

Now we define the $D$ -module of twisted traces from the universal quantization $\mathcal{A}$ of $X$ .

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
